pre_award_internal_routing_form.content:
The Internal Routing Form (IRF) is a required document that must be submitted before applying for any external funding, preferably two weeks prior to the sponsor's submission deadline. The IRF gives the Office of Research Administration basic information about the Principal Investigator and the funding opportunity, captures certifications regarding Responsible Conduct of Research standards, and confirms supervisory approval to proceed with the project. The IRF is completed via DocuSign; questions can be directed to Ms. Deshun Li (deshun.li@morgan.edu) or ask.ora@morgan.edu, 443-885-4044 (fax 443-885-8280).

The IRF includes the following sections:
- MSU Principal Investigator details: name, school, department, contact information.
- Funding Opportunity information: FOA URL, program name, CFDA/ALN number, sponsor type, and due date.
- Application details: project title, MSU role, work location, submission type, activity type, funding amounts, and proposed start date.
- Partner PI & Institution information: required only for subawards.
- Restrictions: six surety questions covering federal/state bar status, criminal convictions, indictments, foreign nationals, and conflicts of interest.
- Requirements: cost share, resource needs, equipment purchases, utilities, personnel, human subjects research, animal research, radioactive materials, and faculty release time.
- Certification statements: affirm project discussion with department leadership, accuracy of information, and acceptance of scientific responsibility.

After the IRF is submitted, the PI must send a Budget (Excel) and Budget Justification (Word) to the ORA Budget Specialist (see the Budget Development page). The IRF must collect signatures from the PI/PD, Department Chair, Dean or Center Director, ORA Research Budget Specialist, Grants Manager, and Director of Research Administration.

DocuSign links:
- PowerForm: https://powerforms.docusign.net/d952f118-fd7b-4b18-b238-57855dc939f7?env=na2&acct=91e00bed-fb84-48ab-9c47-f3a2c0621225&accountId=91e00bed-fb84-48ab-9c47-f3a2c0621225
- Complete new IRF: https://na2.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=d952f118-fd7b-4b18-b238-57855dc939f7&env=na2&acct=91e00bed-fb84-48ab-9c47-f3a2c0621225&v=2

Cost share on the IRF: answer YES or NO — if YES, cost share requires PRE-APPROVAL from ORA. The three types the form asks about are in-kind time (effort), indirect cost (waiver), and cash. Cash cost share is very rare and requires pre-approval.

MSU Share of Funding: if 100% of the request is for MSU, repeat the Total Funding ($) Requested here, including funds to be sent to subawardees. If MSU is the subawardee, enter the dollar amount projected for just MSU.

Partner Role in the Application options: Prime, Subawardee, Equal Collaborator (NSF-only), or Other.

Faculty release time: if YES, enter EACH faculty member requesting release time under the project's funds, including NAME, ROLE, and PERCENTAGE (%) of effort requested.

Foreign nationals: a foreign national is defined as any person who is not a U.S. citizen by birth or naturalization.

Radioactive materials and devices: the form asks separately whether the project involves radioactive materials and whether it involves use of a radioactive device. The PI must be authorized if the answer is YES to either.

Surety questions include whether the applicant has been convicted in the preceding three years of any offense listed in 2 CFR part 180.800(a), or had a civil judgement for one of those offenses within that period.

staff_keyshawn_moncrieffe.content:
Dr. Keyshawn Moncrieffe, PhD is the Director for Research Compliance, Research & Economic Development.

Office: Tyler Hall, Suite 304. Phone: 443-885-1313. Email: keyshawn.moncrieffe@morgan.edu.

Dr. Keyshawn Moncrieffe serves as Director for Research Compliance at Morgan State University. She provides oversight of programs that promote ethical and compliant research — including human research protections (IRB), responsible conduct of research (RCR), financial conflict of interest, export controls, and research security.

She plays a key role in developing the University's inaugural Research Security Program under the NSF-funded Research Integrity, Security, and Compliance (RISC) initiative, in partnership with several Mid-Atlantic Minority Serving Institutions (MSIs).

Dr. Moncrieffe brings extensive experience in research administration, compliance program operations, and project management, advancing Morgan State's mission to foster a culture of research integrity and excellence.

Education: PhD in Higher Education (Advanced Studies Leadership & Policy), Morgan State University; MBA, Morgan State University; MHS, University of Maryland, Baltimore (pending).

Certifications: Certified Research Administrator (CRA) (Research Administrators Certification Council; Certified Compliance & Ethics Professional (CCEP) (Society of Corporate Compliance & Ethics.

Certificates: Contract Administration (Villanova University); Research Administration (University of Maryland, Baltimore); Global Research Ethics (University of Maryland, Baltimore).

staff_farin_kamangar.content:
Farin Kamangar, MD, PhD, CRA is the Associate Vice President for Research, University Distinguished Professor.

Office: Tyler Hall, Suite 304. Phone: 443-885-3447. Email: farin.kamangar@morgan.edu.

Dr. Farin Kamangar is a University Distinguished Professor and Associate Vice President for Research at Morgan State University. He leads the Office of Research Administration and oversees the University's research strategy and externally sponsored research portfolio.

Dr. Kamangar is a cancer epidemiologist and has published over 280 peer-reviewed articles, many in top-tier journals such as The Lancet, BMJ, Annals of Internal Medicine, Lancet Oncology, Journal of Clinical Oncology, Journal of the National Cancer Institute, and Gastroenterology.

He has served as PI or co-PI on over $60 million of NIH-funded projects, including the ASCEND Training Model to Enhance the Diversity of the Biomedical Research Workforce, as well as major epidemiologic studies including the Golestan Cohort Study — a large cohort of over 50,000 individuals with over 20 years of follow-up.

He is a Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) and has received the NIH Merit Award (group award) and the NCI Director's Innovation Award.

Dr. Kamangar has collaborated with researchers at the NIH, Johns Hopkins, the University of Maryland, the International Agency for Research on Cancer, and Tehran University of Medical Sciences.

He has a passion for teaching and mentoring across all levels — from high school to doctoral — with significant experience mentoring minority students.

Education: PhD in Epidemiology, Johns Hopkins University; MHS in Biostatistics, Johns Hopkins University; MPH, Tehran University of Medical Sciences; MD, Tehran University of Medical Sciences.

Certifications: Certified Research Administrator (CRA) (Research Administrators Certification Council; Certified Financial Research Administrator (CFRA) (Research Administrators Certification Council; Certified Pre-Award Research Administrator (CPRA) (Research Administrators Certification Council.

Certificates: Organizational Leadership (Harvard Business School); Financial Accounting (Harvard Business School); Economics (Harvard Business School).

Research interests: Clinical research; Cancer epidemiology; Cardiovascular disease epidemiology; Clinical trials; Epidemiology of esophageal and gastric cancers; Carcinogenicity of opium use; Exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons; Consumption of hot beverages; Effects of opium use on cardiovascular diseases.

Awards: Fellow, American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS); NIH Merit Award (group award); NCI Director's Innovation Award.

Major grants: ASCEND Training Model to Enhance the Diversity of the Biomedical Research Workforce (NIH); Golestan Cohort Study (>50,000 participants, 20+ years follow-up).

trainings_spark.content:
SPARK — Sponsored Projects Administration Readiness and Knowledge — is ORA's training program for Morgan State University RESEARCH STAFF AND ADMINISTRATORS. It is not a proposal-writing program for faculty PIs.

ORA's SPARK program prepares Morgan State University's research staff and administrators for success by building foundational knowledge, practical skills, and confidence in supporting sponsored projects. SPARK introduces participants to key processes, expectations, and institutional practices while creating a pathway for continued learning. It is a scalable framework for MSU research administrator readiness.

TWO-PRONGED APPROACH. (1) A foundational overview of the federal, state, and sponsor-specific requirements that guide sponsored-programs administration and help ensure MSU maintains compliance. (2) A series of practical modules that explain the specific key processes, systems, and institutional workflows involved in administering sponsored programs at Morgan State University.

HOW PROGRESS IS TRACKED. ORA monitors participant progress through attendance at research administration (RA) review sessions, completion of assigned Canvas modules, and submission of the ORA SPARK pre- and post-assessments. Together these confirm that participants have satisfied program requirements. Canvas is the learning management system of record for SPARK.

ONBOARDING (initial phase). A structured introduction to research administration through a blend of self-paced and live learning. Participants complete e-learning modules with associated quizzes, the CITI Essentials of Research Administration course, and virtual RA intensives focused on key topics in the profession.

CITI PROGRAM. Through CITI, SPARK offers the Essentials of Research Administration course, an overview introduction to the profession in five lessons: Elements of Research Administration; Elements of Research Development; Elements of Pre-Award; Elements of Award Negotiation & Acceptance; Elements of Post Award. (This is a different CITI course from the HSR/RCR/COI compliance training.)

SPARK CAMPFIRE SERIES. Focused ONE-HOUR learning sessions on key topics in research administration, combining practical instruction with discussion and Q&A. Topics may include cost share, Uniform Guidance, compensation on sponsored projects, financial compliance and expense monitoring, subaward establishment and monitoring, research compliance, export controls, research security, IRB, IACUC, and other timely or high-priority areas. The series aims to foster a community of research administration professionals across campus.

SPARK e-LEARNING MODULES. ORA's training staff developed a series of e-learning modules tailored to the administration of research at Morgan State. Seven modules, 3 hours 40 minutes in total:

  1. Navigating Banner: Essentials for Research Administration (30 min) — Banner access; grant indexes and budget pools; available budget balances; payroll and fringe visibility; Banner/Argos reporting tools; award budget structure; key award information; labor and cost redistributions.
  2. Purchasing with Purpose: Procurement on Sponsored Projects (45 min) — procurement roles and responsibilities; allowability and allocability; purchasing thresholds; P-card considerations; vendor setup; requisition processing; documentation; working fund administration.
  3. Travel on Sponsored Projects: Approval to Reimbursement (30 min) — travel allowability; pre-approval requirements; sponsor and institutional rules; airfare, lodging, meals and mileage; documentation standards; reimbursement process; common compliance concerns.
  4. Supporting Participants: Payments, Benefits, and Indirect Costs (30 min) — participant support costs including stipends, tuition, travel and healthcare; participant support restrictions; indirect cost impact; rebudgeting considerations.
  5. Building the Project Team: Contractual Hiring and Compensation (45 min) — contractual hiring; compensation allowability; institutional base salary considerations; secondary contract rules; release time requests; EPAF submissions; labor allocability; faculty summer contract calculations.
  6. Show Your Work: Understanding Time and Effort Reporting (30 min) — effort reporting under Uniform Guidance; SearchLight process; certification responsibilities; percent effort allocation; audit risk.
  7. It Takes a Village: Understanding Cost Share on Sponsored Projects (30 min) — mandatory vs. voluntary committed cost share; tracking; documentation requirements; allowable cost share sources; third-party contributions.

These are the same modules published as ORA eTraining; the eighth eTraining module, Post Award Quick Guide, is not listed in the SPARK table.

HOW TO JOIN. Complete ORA's Google Form to express interest in the SPARK program. SPARK is currently only available to employees of Morgan State University, and a valid MSU email address is required to complete the form.

trainings_e_training.content:
The Office of Research Administration (ORA) is pleased to provide a gamut of training modules touching on all aspects of administrative functions here at Morgan State University. The eTraining catalog consists of eight self-paced modules covering the full spectrum of post-award and grant operations work.

Available eTraining modules:

1) Post Award Quick Guide — Covers establishing award guidelines, determining allowable costs, setting up awards in Banner, compliance matters, reporting requirements, prior approvals, and resources.

2) Navigating Banner: Essentials for Research Administration — Provides an overview of reviewing grant-funded activity, budget review, encumbrances, budget transfers, and cost transfers in Banner.

3) Building the Project Team: Contractual Hiring and Compensation — Addresses hiring staff, summer research contracts, and honoraria processing.

4) Travel on Sponsored Projects: Approval to Reimbursement — Covers travel authorization requests, reimbursement claims, and compliance rules.

5) Purchasing with Purpose: Procurement on Sponsored Projects / Banner Pool Level 08 — Covers vendor goods/services, requisitions, and subawards.

6) Supporting Participants: Payments, Benefits, and Indirect Costs — Addresses participant stipends, tuition, healthcare, travel, indirect costs, and Modified Total Direct Costs (MTDC).

7) Show Your Work: Understanding Time and Effort Reporting — Explains the time/effort certification process for faculty, staff, and students.

8) It Takes a Village: Understanding Cost Share on Sponsored Projects — Covers cost share types, approval processes, and documentation.

These modules are intended for faculty, principal investigators, department admins, and research staff who manage or interact with sponsored projects. The page does not specify required vs. encouraged designations, login procedures, or fixed cadence — the modules are evergreen/self-service.

Additional details revealed by Playwright: Each of the 8 modules has a direct Articulate Rise URL exposed through expandable accordion panels. The interactive Rise modules are hosted at rise.articulate.com or share.articulate.com and open in a new tab. Direct URLs: (1) Post Award Quick Guide — https://rise.articulate.com/share/bLJYTO9HcIsvOpsVS9KKkClk3VoLSs1N (with 9 sub-modules: establishing guidelines from Notice of Award, allowable costs/activities, Banner setup and spending instruments, audit-risk expenses, compliance, reporting, prior approval, ORA resources, MSU responsible officers); (2) Navigating Banner — https://rise.articulate.com/share/JssRlmP10hNJXNgv9sqeHN86eYaosJ7S; (3) Building the Project Team — https://rise.articulate.com/share/SYMnLxQyzAquu3LhTIbEIQ2_VQdKfFWH (Banner pool 02: Contractual Salaries); (4) Travel on Sponsored Projects — https://rise.articulate.com/share/EkNni5Bgg6Epa2bjN00d_owxwj1AFjeC (covers MSU policy + Uniform Guidance rules for travel authorization & reimbursement); (5) Purchasing with Purpose (Banner Pool 08: Grant-Funded Contractual Services) — https://rise.articulate.com/share/5gROiZqb81HR0jfGreHGt00baHxOl2m2 (vendor goods/services, Banner requisitions, subawards); (6) Supporting Participants — https://share.articulate.com/fLyvCDI1vSeMFtSyq2ebF (stipends, tuition, healthcare, travel, indirect costs, MTDC); (7) Show Your Work: Time and Effort — https://share.articulate.com/s01WpXKAGFN1dft3QDlow (note: distinct from the D-RED Time & Effort interactive module at rise.articulate.com/share/YUeYo_t7gEEPZQPjwbuFNy3UD03HIsYQ); (8) It Takes a Village: Cost Share — https://share.articulate.com/jQ-qp8p2axC-3ba_0hXae (types of cost share, approvals, documentation, Banner cost share activity code).

Contact for eTraining questions: Office of Research Administration, Tyler Hall, Student Service Bldg, Suite 304, Baltimore, MD 21251. Phone 443-885-4044. Email ask.ora@morgan.edu.

trainings_monthly_d_red.content:
The Monthly D-RED Seminars are a recurring monthly training series hosted by ORA on research administration topics. The page does not spell out what 'D-RED' stands for, but the seminars are organized by the Division of Research and Economic Development under which ORA sits. Sessions are open to MSU faculty, researchers, and staff interested in research funding, compliance, and administration topics. The schedule pattern is typically the second Wednesday of each month (recent dates fall on Sep 10, Oct 9, Nov 12, Dec 11). Each session is recorded via Zoom and slide decks (PDFs) are archived.

post_award_notification_and_setup.content:
Notification of Award: Award notifications may take the form of an award letter, a purchase order, a detailed contract, or an agreement spelling out the terms and conditions. The notification is directed to the Assistant VP for Research Administration, who distributes copies to the PI/PD and the VP for Finance and Management. The Office of Restricted Funds Accounting (RFA) is also notified.

Important: Awards for proposals that did not undergo the normal internal processing, review, and approval through the Office of Research Administration (ORA) may be refused by the University.

Set-Up of Award: Once the award is formally accepted, documents are forwarded to RFA, which assigns an Index or Budget code number and establishes the account in Banner (the University's financial system). The Comptroller's Office is notified. Account setup typically takes up to three (3) business days. A Post-Award Briefing meeting is then scheduled with the PI and supporting units.

Post-Award Briefing: The Post-Award Briefing provides a roadmap in administering and managing key grant/contract post-award activities, spanning from account setup through final reporting. Primary offices involved in the briefing are:
- Office of Research Administration (ORA)
- Office of Human Resources
- Office of Procurement
- Office of the Comptroller
- Purchasing Card Office

Contacts: ORA — Tyler Hall, Student Service Bldg, Suite 304, Baltimore, MD 21251. Phone 443-885-4044. Fax 443-885-8280. Email ask.ora@morgan.edu. Research Compliance Director: Dr. Edet Isuk — edet.isuk@morgan.edu.

Post-Award Briefing contact: Mr. Ryan Mobley, Training and Communications Coordinator, Office of Research Administration — ask.ora@morgan.edu.

post_award_changes_to_an_award.content:
Changes to an Award covers procedures for modifying active sponsored research awards at Morgan State University. Prior to planning for any changes in a received award, review the award document and sponsor policies to determine approval requirements.

Types of changes covered:

1. Change of PI or Key Personnel — Requires approval from the department head, dean, and sponsor. The request package must include the CV of the new PI or Co-PI. Requests are routed through the Associate Vice President for Research, Dr. Farin Kamangar.

2. No Cost Extension (NCE) — The PI must notify ORA in writing at least 60 days before the project's expiration date. ORA will work with the PI to obtain the sponsor's approval.

3. Transfer of Award FROM Another Institution (incoming) — Requires sponsor approval and approval from the previous institution. The PI submits a new or revised proposal package through ORA.

4. Transfer of Award TO Another Institution (outgoing) — If MSU retains the project, a new PI is appointed. If MSU releases the project, the departing PI must request transfer approval from the department head, dean, and sponsor. A final accounting and certification is required before the transfer can be completed.

Additional details: When MSU elects to retain a project after the PI departs, the departing PI may continue to be retained on the project through either a subaward or a consultant agreement. Outgoing transfers are approved only after final accounting and certification by the responsible grant accountant that all incurred obligations have been settled and that a remaining balance exists for transfer.

Contact: Office of Research Administration, Tyler Hall, Student Service Bldg, Suite 304, Baltimore, MD 21251. Phone 443-885-4044. Fax 443-885-8280. Email ask.ora@morgan.edu.

pre_award_overview.content:
Morgan State University requires all sponsored project proposals to undergo review and approval through the Office of Research Administration (ORA). The Pre-Award section provides information and resources for complete proposal development, including preparation tools, institutional data, sponsor information, and necessary forms. Faculty, PIs, and research staff can reach ORA at ask.ora@morgan.edu or by phone at 443-885-4044.

Proposal development process: Resources include PI Handbooks, trainings, and access to the Pivot-RP Funding Opportunities Database (https://pivot.proquest.com/dashboard). Researchers should review proposal components and the submission checklist, then develop budgets according to university guidelines. ORA offers tips for timely proposal submission presented by staff specialists.

Intention to submit: An Internal Routing Form (IRF) initiates the proposal review process and should be submitted at least two weeks before the agency deadline. Concurrent submission of the budget (Excel format) and the budget justification (Word format) to designated ORA staff is required.

Application information available on this site: University application information (UEI, EIN, NAICS, SAM expiration, etc.), the current fringe benefit rate schedule, and the Facilities & Administrative (F&A) cost rates are all documented resources for proposal budgeting. Ms. Deshun Li and Ailing Zhang, MS are referenced as ORA pre-award contacts. Pre-award spending information and advance account creation are addressed in a dedicated section, and pre-award subaward procedures are covered separately. A Limited Submission policy applies when sponsors cap how many proposals MSU may submit.

Subpages: University Application Information, Role of Principal Investigator, Proposal Components, Proposal Submission Checklist, Internal Routing Form, Budget Development, Fringe Benefit Rate, F&A Cost Rates, Proposal and Budget Examples, Pre-Award Spending, Pre-Award Subawards, and Limited Submission.

Pivot-RP Funding Opportunities Database: use your Morgan email address on sign up.

pre_award_role_of_principal_investigator.content:
This page explains who is eligible to serve as Principal Investigator (PI) or Project Director (PD) on a sponsored project at Morgan State University. For questions, contact the Office of Research Administration at ask.ora@morgan.edu or 443-885-4044.

Eligibility categories:
- Full-time tenure track faculty members at any academic rank automatically qualify as PI/PD.
- Other university appointees (directors, senior administrators, visiting faculty, retired faculty) may serve as PI/PD with dean approval. A formal Memorandum of Designation must be filed with ORA. Adjunct faculty serving as PI/PD may need a full-time co-PI/PD.
- Full-time regular staff with appropriate qualifications are eligible to serve as PI/PD.
- Individual fellowship applications: when a sponsor requires the Fellow to be the PI/PD, a Sponsor or Mentor meeting the criteria above will serve as the Project Director on MSU records and handle administrative and scientific oversight of the award.

post_award_forms_index.content:
The Post-Award Forms page lists the eight DocuSign forms required for grant-funded requests processed through the Morgan State University Office of Research Administration (ORA). All submissions route through DocuSign to the MSU ORA signing group; questions and submissions go to ora-docusign@morgan.edu.

Forms available (each has its own form card in the KB):

1. Honoraria Request Memo — payment for participation to a person not employed by or a student of Morgan State University. One-time payments with market-rate limitations. International payments require Accounts Payable guidance.

2. PF-10 Contractual Personnel Request Form — exclusively for revisions and continuation requests for existing contractual personnel. New employees must use the EPAF system via WebSIS.

3. Stipend Request Memo — the Check Issue Date should ideally be at least 30 days out from the date the memo is submitted; contact ask.ora@morgan.edu if an earlier date is required. Covers both non-Title III and Title III funded stipends.

4. Non-Title III Travel Request Form — for grant travel funded by non-Title III sources. As of 05/30/2024, 'Grant/Award End Date' is a mandatory field. Additional details at the University Travel website.

5. Title III Travel Request Form — for grant travel funded by Title III sources.

6. Travel Reimbursement Form (GAD Form X-5) — uses the State of Maryland Expense Account (GAD Form X-5) format.

7. Grant-Funded Undergraduate Tuition, Fees, and Health Insurance Request Memo — for undergraduate tuition, fees, and health insurance support paid from grant funds.

8. Grant-Funded Graduate Tuition and Fees Request Memo — graduate version; graduate student health insurance must be reimbursed via a separate requisition, not on this memo.

General guidance and references: PI Handbook 3: Grant-Related Processes (2025-02-24 PDF) documents the broader post-award business processes these forms support.

Additional details (verified via Playwright on 2026-05-14): The live page now lists the primary DocuSign forms contact as Rebecca Steiner (rebecca.steiner@morgan.edu, 443-885-4044) — the older ora-docusign@morgan.edu inbox may still be monitored but is not displayed on the current page. The two travel request forms (Title III and Non-Title III) are grouped on the live page under the heading 'Travel Request Form (COMP 01)', which is the State of Maryland COMP-01 form designation. For PF-10 guidance on first-time and repeat employees (who use EPAF via WebSIS instead), an ORA e-training module on Contractual Salaries is available at https://www.morgan.edu/office-of-research-administration/trainings/e-training. Travel form completion guidance and TL-number processing tips are at https://www.morgan.edu/comptroller/university-travel (questions to the Office of the Comptroller's Travel Division). A completed sample of the Undergraduate Tuition memo is published at https://www.morgan.edu/Documents/ADMINISTRATION/OFFICES/ora/ORAForms/Post-Award%20Forms/Samples/Sample_UndergradTuition.pdf (KB doc_id: form_sample_undergrad_tuition_memo).
